newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones results flat; to invest in Telerate.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones results flat; to invest in Telerate.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co. Inc., reporting flat earnings for the fourth quarter and full year, said Monday it expects to spend up to $650 million over the next three to four years to revitalise and expand Dow Jones Telerate, its global financial information services unit.
Wall Street investors reacted to the news by pushing the company's stock down $3.375 to $37.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Dow Jones, a diversified financial services and publishing company, reported fourth-quarter earnings of $59.6 million, or 62 cents per share, compared with year-ago profits of $59.9 million, or 62 cents a share. Revenues rose to $671 million from $612 million.

For the year, the publisher of The Wall Street Journal and Barron's earned $189.9 million, or $1.96 a share, on revenues of $2.48 billion. In 1995 it earned $189.6 million, or $1.96 a share, on revenues of $2.28 billion.

According to First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings outlooks, the consensus for the latest quarter was 60 cents per share and $1.84 for the full year. For 1997, First Call has projected earnings of $1.94 a share.
The company estimated that after the Telerate costs, 1997 earnings will be between $1.20 and $1.40 per share, and said its 1998 results also will be affected by the programme.

The business publishing segment, which includes the company's print publications, television operations and Business Information Services group, posted a full-year revenue increase of 15.7 percent to just over $1.2 billion.
Revenues at Dow Jones' financial information services unit, which includes the Dow Jones Telerate and Financial News Services groups, advanced 1.9 percent to $979.7 million.
Ottaway Newspapers, Inc., the company's community newspaper subsidiary, reported a 5.4 percent revenue gain to $287.5 million.
